module: Exports the player's vehicle in glTF 2.0 format (.gltf with JSON or binary .glb), or a keyframe sequence. It fetches the vehicle's GPU mesh (GPUMesh.bng_getGPUMesh) then writes the buffers (vertices, normals, tangents, UVs, colors, indices), the flexbodies and props, the JBeam part tree (as a hierarchy of glTF nodes), the materials (textures converted to PNG, BeamNG material data in extras.bngMaterial) and, if exportBeams is true, the nodes and beams of each part (BNG_JBeamData extension). The vehicle direction is written in the BNG_Direction extension. Coordinates are converted to {x, z, -y}. The export is asynchronous: it happens in updateGFX when the GPU data is ready. Useful to import a BeamNG vehicle into Blender or another 3D tool.

embedBuffers.desc: true (default): buffers embedded in base64 in the JSON; false: external .bin files (<name>_buffer_NNN_<type>.bin). Ignored in binary format.

gltfBinaryFormat.desc: true (default): writes a .glb; false: writes a JSON .gltf

exportTexCoords.desc: Exports both texture coordinate sets (default false)

exportBeams.desc: Exports the nodes and beams per part in extras (default true)

notes: The export takes player vehicle 0 in its current state (deformations included: current node positions for the beams).
export(handler): if an export is already in progress (lastMeshInfo not nil), the handler is called with nil and nothing else is done.
startRecording writes a first frame then keeps exporting every frame until stopRecording; the times are stored in a glTF animation. The output logs each frame.
suggestFilename looks for export_001 to export_100 in the vehicle's folder, with the .glb or .gltf extension depending on gltfBinaryFormat; if all exist, returns the last name tested.

Bug: in _addTimeBuffers, the keyframe number buffer uses the variable bufferID (undefined, so nil) instead of bufferIDKeyframes, and the max time bound uses keyFrameTimes[#keyFrameTimes - 1]. Animation recording is therefore probably incorrect.
Bug: in _convertType, `dumps(value)" to "` (missing .. operator) is a function call on a string and would cause a Lua error in conversion error cases.

Bug: _isTextureCookerFilepath tests `not string.sub(filepath, -4) == ".png"`, an expression that is always false in practice (precedence of the not operator); the extension test is therefore not done.
After an export, the GUI hook ThreeDExported is triggered and a "GLTF Vehicle exported" message is displayed for 5 s.

export.desc: Starts the player vehicle export and calls handler(gltfRoot) with the built glTF table when the GPU data is ready (in updateGFX).

handler.desc: Function receiving the root glTF table (or nil if an export is already in progress)

exportFile.desc: Exports the player vehicle to a glTF file (JSON or binary depending on gltfBinaryFormat). Resets the image cache and displays an interface message.

startRecording.desc: Exports a first frame to the file then keeps exporting every frame (animation) until stopRecording is called.

stopRecording.desc: Stops the animation recording started by startRecording.

updateGFX.desc: Hook called every frame: if the mesh GPU data is ready, finishes the export in progress (processExport).

suggestFilename.desc: Suggests a free file name export_NNN.glb or .gltf in the player vehicle's folder (for the interface).

returns.desc: Suggested path, or empty string if there is no player vehicle

getGeInfo.desc: Returns the export settings useful to the interface (currently only gltfBinaryFormat).
